summary: The local who knows every door: {local operator}, who knows the district's families and doubted you, offers to work for you after hearing you speak where you did not expect anyone to listen.
realLife: In Kennedy's 1946 House race in Boston, Dave Powers, a Charlestown man who knew the district and had doubted a rich Harvard man, joined after hearing him speak to mothers who had lost sons in the war, and stayed with him until 1963.
gates: A person on record with ties across the district who is with no campaign.
They attended an event where you spoke.
weights: How far your background is from the district's.
choices: ask them to run your days and your doors
thank them and keep your own people

branches.when: they doubted you as a rich outsider
branches.then: They say so first. Whether you answer it decides how hard they work.

branches.when: they complain that politicians never knock
branches.then: They take you door to door on their own streets, which opens doors no list would.
They stay for years, a staff tie later scenes read.
